title: SL vs ENG Tri-Series: Kusal Mendis Wins Toss And Opts To Bowl First In 3rd ODI At Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium
text:

 Kusal Mendis has won the toss and opted to bowl first in the 3rd ODI of the ongoing tri-nation series in Pakistan. Both the teams have lost their previous games against the hosts Pakistan.
 by Chetan Phore | Oct 22, 2026 | 2 mins read Mendis and Brook during the toss in Rawalpindi · Credits: Via SLC Cricket Sri Lankan skipper Kusal Mendis has won the toss against the England skipper Harry Brook and has opted to bowl first in the 3rd ODI of the ongoing tri-series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi, on the 22nd of October, 2026. This tri nation series is being held in Pakistan as it includes the home side also.
 “We will bowl first. The pitch looks fresh and we want to maximize any early movement or moisture available in the opening hour. Getting some early wickets will put them under pressure. It’s a crucial match for us to stay alive in this tri-series, and the boys are focused on putting up a disciplined bowling performance,” Kusal Mendis said after winning the toss.

 “We would have probably looked at the overhead conditions, but we are happy to bat first as well. It looks like a good surface that will remain consistent. We didn't quite get going in our previous chase against Pakistan, so setting a target gives our batting unit a clear path today. We need to build solid partnerships through the middle overs,” Harry Brooks after losing the toss.
 Sri Lanka Playing XI
 Avishka Fernando, Kamindu Mendis, Kusal Mendis (captain and wicketkeeper), Pavan Rathnayake, Sahan Arachchige, Janith Liyanage, Dasun Shanaka, Dunith Wellalage, Eshan Malinga, Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka
 England Playing XI
 Tom Banton, Ben Duckett, Joe Root, Harry Brook (captain), Jordan Cox (wicketkeeper), Will Jacks, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, Jamie Overton, Gus Atkinson, Josh Tongue
 Last match of both the teams
 Sri Lanka lost their last match against the hosts Pakistan four days ago as they were defeated by 37 runs. Pakistani batter Salman Ali Agha scored an impressive century which took Pakistan’s total to 305. Sri Lanka failed to chase the total as they were bowled out for 268. Eshan Malinga’s 4 wickets went in vain as the Lankan batters collapsed horribly in the death overs.
 On the other hand, England also lost their last match to the hosts Pakistan by 87 runs two days ago. Pakistan posted a total of 302 in their 50 overs. England batters Tom Banton and Ben Duckett played well by scoring 57 and 45 runs respectively but their middle order could not stand in the crease and hence England were bowled out for 215. Arafat Minhas was the star of the Pakistan bowling as he recorded a figure of 6/40.
